data.narrative:
Lydian is a Series A climate and energy company that has raised $62.1M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of nine peers in the Climate & Energy sector, including one public company (LNZA) and eight private firms such as Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

The stage-progression method is applicable here, using the $62.1M total raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression to the next financing stage. This yields an implied valuation of $124M. A peer-median approach was not viable; while eight same-sector peers exist, none of the narrow filters—same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier—yielded the minimum three comparable datapoints required for statistical reliability. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material bias.

The triangulated analysis, constrained to a single applicable method, supports a range of $106M (low) to $143M (high), with a median of $124M. This range reflects a ±15% band around the stage-progression midpoint. Key uncertainties include the absence of sufficiently close Stage A peers in climate technology, which limits cross-validation of the 2.0x multiplier assumption for this sector specifically, and the representativeness of total raised as a valuation proxy given market conditions at deployment.
